items.title: tinyhumansai/openhuman: The fastest, cheapest, most efficient open-source agent harness.
items.snippet: The fastest, cheapest, most efficient open-source agent harness, OpenHuman, allows running over 500 agents on a $10 VPS. Its core is compiled Rust, ensuring low memory and CPU usage between model calls. The system also features deeply integrated memory and RLM token compression for efficiency.

items.title: PostgreSQL RPM repository meets AI with pg_statviz
items.snippet: pg_statviz now integrates with LLMs like Claude, Ollama, OpenAI, or Gemini to explain PostgreSQL statistics across various distributions. This tool, updated on October 12, 2026, snapshots internal statistics and generates charts, enhancing database analysis with AI insights. Getting there took three days and a few dozen new Python packages.

items.title: From Given to Gathered Evidence: Agentic Learning for Longitudinal Medical Reasoning
items.snippet: Org profile for CASE on Hugging Face, the AI community building the future. (This paper introduces agentic learning for longitudinal medical reasoning, focusing on the ability of AI agents to gather and utilize evidence over time for complex medical tasks. This research contributes to advancing automated reasoning and decision-making in the healthcare domain.)

items.title: Understanding neural circuit principles for representation learning through joint-embedding predictive architectures
items.snippet: This work establishes a circuit-centric theory framework for understanding how the brain may acquire an internal model of the world through experience. The model learns sequence representations resembling successor-like representations observed in the human primary visual cortex and develops abstract sequence representations comparable to those in the macaque prefrontal cortex.

items.title: Let your AI agent operate
items.snippet: fortrabbit empowers AI agents with an MCP server, public API, CLI, and dedicated agent skills, facilitating autonomous operation and project management. A demonstration illustrates an agent utilizing these tools to initiate projects, synchronize files, manage databases, and establish environments efficiently.

dropped.title: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
dropped.snippet: Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes. A replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there's no centralized point to shut off—though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days).
